papers.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
papers.problem: Chat-style video generators with small chunks answer fast but look worse than large-chunk models.
papers.fix: Speculative Sampling pads the window with noise and caches predictions, so large-window models respond fast without extra training.
papers.practicalUseCase: Fast video apps no longer need small chunks, so try large windows and speed up each chunk instead.
papers.limitation: The excerpt gives no speed numbers, so the size of the gain stays unknown.

papers.title: FreeSolo: Linear-time Sparse Attention with Zero-Shot Length Extrapolation
papers.problem: Models that read long text in linear time forget details, and full attention costs far too much.
papers.fix: FreeSolo reads nearby text plus selected key points, and it extends to longer text than training without fine-tuning.
papers.practicalUseCase: Long documents may cost less to process, so watch for models that use this sparse design.
papers.limitation: The excerpt gives no speed or accuracy numbers, so the size of the gain stays unknown.

papers.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
papers.problem: Cutting parts from reasoning models makes their accuracy collapse on long, hard problems like AIME.
papers.fix: LayerTrim trims only redundant layer features without training, lifting accuracy up to 21.4 points and cutting peak GPU memory 19.7%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Smaller reasoning models can run cheaper on your own GPU, so try this trimming before you buy more hardware.
papers.limitation: Tests covered three reasoning models and five benchmarks, and it won in most settings, not all.

papers.title: Lluna: Collaborative Unimodal Models for Missing-Modality Inference
papers.problem: Combined models can become less accurate than a single model when some input types go missing.
papers.fix: Lluna adds a direct single-input path beside the shared branch and improves average missing-input scores by 4.26% across eight datasets.
papers.practicalUseCase: Real apps often lose sensor or text inputs, so keep a direct single-input path in multi-input models.
papers.limitation: The 4.26% gain is an average against the strongest baseline tested, not against every possible method.

papers.title: Looking Complete Is Not Being Grounded: Evaluating LLM Sitreps Against Human-Authored Situation Reports
papers.problem: Teams judge AI crisis reports with text-overlap scores that do not measure what aid workers need.
papers.fix: AI reports match the human score (0.827 versus 0.821), but copy only 5.4-11.0% of official figures.
papers.practicalUseCase: AI crisis reports look complete but lack verified facts, so check their numbers and sources before you trust them.
papers.limitation: The tie with humans did not repeat under a second judge model, and it covers five disasters.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks form sustainability committees, but it is unclear whether those committees change anything real.
papers.fix: Committees raise green scores at all banks, but at Islamic banks they lift only overall and resource scores, not products.
papers.practicalUseCase: A committee alone may only signal effort at Islamic banks, so check for green products and innovations too.
papers.limitation: Panel regressions show links in emerging markets, so they do not prove the committees caused the changes.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little is known about how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what decides issue size.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk from 2012 to 2022, sustainability sukuk stay tiny and cluster in Indonesia, Malaysia and Saudi Arabia.
papers.practicalUseCase: Bigger issues use equity-based contracts, so issuers should pick those and weigh the cost of second party opinions.
papers.limitation: The data covers 2012 to 2022 and shows links between traits and issue size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lack proof that AI and big data actually improve their results.
papers.fix: AI use, data analytics and data management all raise bank competitiveness and sustainable development in a survey of 214 managers.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks that invest in AI and data tools gain an edge, so fund those before extra staff digital training.
papers.limitation: The data comes from one country in a single-time survey, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in dual systems lack clear evidence on what drives their growth.
papers.fix: ICT adoption is the strongest growth driver across 218 Islamic and conventional banks, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks should invest in digital systems first, because exports and institutions add less on their own.
papers.limitation: The data covers 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, and it shows links, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries leave people outside formal finance, even as Islamic finance grows.
papers.fix: In OIC countries, income, tertiary education, institutional quality, internet access, population and age dependency all shape financial inclusion.
papers.practicalUseCase: Unlike OECD countries, OIC countries must invest heavily in digital systems, youth and women, and raise incomes.
papers.limitation: The model covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students fear being exposed as incompetent, but nobody had pooled how often it happens.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings are frequent among medical students before they get licensed, according to a pooled review of studies.
papers.practicalUseCase: Impostor feelings are common in high-pressure training, so expect them in yourself and talk about them early.
papers.limitation: Results varied widely across studies and sampling methods, so the pooled rate is uncertain.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students use generative AI heavily, but it is unclear what drives their innovative research.
papers.fix: Inner drive and outside rewards both lift doctoral students' innovation, and unmet basic psychological needs sharply reduce it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Research support, resources and confidence help most when motivation is weak, so build those and protect your motivation.
papers.limitation: The survey used self-reports from one time point in chemistry, so it cannot prove cause.
